sn12.53:1.2: “Bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating gratification in things that can fetter, craving increases.
sn12.53:1.3: With craving as condition, clinging comes to be;
sn12.53:1.6: with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair come to be.
sn12.53:1.7: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.53:2.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, an oil lamp was burning in dependence on oil and a wick,
sn12.53:2.2: and a man would pour oil into it and adjust the wick from time to time.
sn12.53:2.3: Thus, sustained by that oil, fuelled by it, that oil lamp would burn for a very long time.
sn12.53:2.4: So too, when one lives contemplating gratification in things that can fetter, craving increases….
sn12.53:2.9: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.53:3.1: “Bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating danger in things that can fetter, craving ceases.
sn12.53:3.2: With the cessation of craving comes cessation of clinging;
sn12.53:3.3: with the cessation of clinging, cessation of existence …
sn12.53:3.5: aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair cease.
sn12.53:3.6: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.53:4.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, an oil lamp was burning in dependence on oil and a wick,
sn12.53:4.2: and the man would not pour oil into it or adjust the wick from time to time.
sn12.53:4.3: Thus, when the former supply of fuel is exhausted, that oil lamp, not being fed with any more fuel, lacking sustenance, would be extinguished.
sn12.53:4.4: So too, when one lives contemplating danger in things that can fetter, craving ceases….
sn12.53:4.6: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
